blocks.content: Biodiversity is the term popularized by the sociobiologist Edward Wilson to describe the combined diversity at all the levels of biological organisation.

rows: On-site conservation of organisms within their natural habitat
Off-site conservation of threatened species outside their natural habitat
Protects the entire ecosystem along with all resident species
Focuses on protecting specific endangered species or gametes
National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Sacred Groves
Zoological Parks, Botanical Gardens, Cryopreservation, Seed Banks
Cost-effective and requires minimal human intervention
High cost requiring specialized facilities and active human maintenance

items: In-situ conservation includes National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves, whereas Ex-situ includes Botanical Gardens, Cryopreservation, and Seed Banks.
Paul Ehrlich proposed the 'Rivet Popper Hypothesis' to illustrate the ecosystem impact of species loss.
The Evil Quartet lists the four primary causes of biodiversity loss, with habitat loss and fragmentation being the most critical.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Biodiversity refers to the sum total of diversity existing at all levels of biological organization: genetic, species, and ecological.
Sociobiologist Edward Wilson popularized the term biodiversity to describe combined diversity across biological levels.
The 'Evil Quartet' driving species extinction includes Habitat Loss & Fragmentation, Over-exploitation, Alien Species Invasions, and Co-extinctions.
Biodiversity hotspots cover less than 2% of Earth's land area but harbour over 50% of endemic terrestrial species.
Conservation strategies are broadly categorized into In-situ (on-site) and Ex-situ (off-site) approaches.
